byteLevelVerification.method: Both fixtures hexdumped and decoded independently of the subject's catalog fields. Prefix decoded as 4-byte big-endian unsigned per the live contract frame clause. Body length compared against the decoded N.

members.verification: N decodes to 0 as a 4-byte big-endian unsigned. The contract frame clause states N counts the body only, not the prefix, so a conforming N=0 frame is exactly the 4 prefix bytes and no body. File is exactly those 4 bytes. The subject's statement 'No JSON body is authored because N counts the body only and is 0' is correct and follows from the closed clause.
members.typingVerification: RF-2 covers names 'length prefix of 0' verbatim as a covered violation, unconditionally and independent of handshake state. preHandshake additionally states 'N equal to 0 is refusal family RF-2, detected from the prefix alone; the receiver must refuse without buffering the body.' The subject's expected outcome quotes both properties and invents neither.
members.isolationTest: The vector trips exactly one RF-2 sub-cause. With zero body bytes there is nothing to parse, so it cannot ambiguously also trip truncated-body, invalid-UTF-8, duplicate-member, unknown-member, or numeric sub-causes. Clean single-predicate fixture.
members.uniquenessTest: Byte-unique. There is exactly one 4-byte big-endian unsigned encoding of 0 and no body to serialize, so CC-11's non-canonical-serialization freedom has no purchase on this member.

members.verification: N decodes to 4 and the body is exactly 4 bytes, so N counts the body only and the frame is well-formed at the framing layer. The body decodes to the ASCII/UTF-8 octets 6e 75 6c 6c, the RFC 8259 null literal, lowercase, with no leading or trailing whitespace. The subject's claim that it is 'the unique RFC 8259 null token with no whitespace' is exact.
members.typingVerification: RF-2 covers names 'non-object top level' verbatim. The live encoding clause states 'A frame body is one UTF-8 JSON text (RFC 8259) whose top level is a single object' and 'a non-object top level rejects'. Under RFC 8259 (unlike RFC 4627) a bare null is a valid JSON text, so this body is a valid JSON text whose top level is not an object - which is precisely the predicate under test. Typing is determined by closed clauses; nothing is invented.
members.isolationTest: The vector trips exactly one RF-2 sub-cause. 'null' is pure ASCII so it cannot also trip invalid-UTF-8; it carries no members so it cannot trip duplicate-member or unknown-member; it carries no numbers so it cannot trip the float/negative/over-uint53 rule; N equals the body length exactly so it cannot trip truncated-body. Clean single-predicate fixture, and notably the minimal one that requires inventing no per-type body schema.
members.handshakeStateTest: The typed outcome is determined in both handshake states without selecting a bound. Pre-handshake, N=4 is neither 0 nor greater than 65536, so the prefix check passes and the body is parsed. Post-handshake, the negotiated bound is at least 65536, so N=4 passes there too. Either way the parse reaches the top-level predicate and rejects. The fixture therefore needs no bound and uses none.
members.familyOrderingTest: Attacked the possibility that a null-bodied frame arriving in AWAIT-HELLO should be typed to a handshake family (RF-1/RF-8) rather than RF-2. Refuted by the contract's own whyOutsideTheFamilyRule clause: 'an RF-2 frame violation is detected before any parse assigns the frame a family'. Parse-level rejection precedes family assignment, so RF-2 is the correct typing in every state. The subject's expected outcome is right.

byteLevelVerification.candidateDiscardPhrase: Both members' expected outcomes end 'Uncommitted candidates discarded.' This is not invented: the live file 08 DR-G21 row names 'candidate discard' in its acceptance-evidence cell, and the row's obligation sentence reads 'One component failure never crashes the core or leaks uncommitted authority.' Grounded in the live row.

decision.scopeOfAccept: Accepts g21-fixture-corpus.v3 as a CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED leftover-design fixture-authoring artifact under D-056 Decision 5, authoring exactly two CC-5 RF-2 injection payloads against already-closed control-protocol-contract.v2 framing. The accept covers the correctness and lawfulness of the two authored byte sequences, the accuracy of every cited digest, and the honesty of the not-authored and remaining-work accounting. It does not record the corpus, does not close leftover-design of OBL-G21-FX-AUTHORING, does not move any file 08 token, and confers no execution or QUALIFIED standing.
decision.rationale: Twenty dispatch attacks and thirteen further independent attacks were run; all thirty-three were refuted against live bytes. The subject and both fixtures are frozen at their expected digests at mode 0444 with no motion across the review, and HEAD is unchanged. All 22 cited path+digest pairs recompute exactly, as do the three cited commit hashes and the naming-parent attribution to D-145. The two payloads were decoded by hand and are correct: 00000000 is the unique 4-byte big-endian zero with no body, and 000000046e756c6c declares N=4 over exactly the 4-byte RFC 8259 null literal. Each is a clean single-predicate vector that trips exactly one covered RF-2 violation and cannot ambiguously trip another, and each has a typed outcome determined identically pre- and post-handshake, so no bound and no undecided value is needed or used. Every framing clause the subject relies on was compared against the live contract; three are verbatim-exact and two are faithfully abridged without distortion. The strongest structural objections available - that non-object top level is absent from CC-5's intent enumeration, and that the input-corpus CC-5 row names a narrower oversize state - were pursued to the class enumeration and the live row, and both fail: CC-5 is the only class whose name and RF-2 typing own the predicate, and the subject draws the oversize distinction explicitly rather than blurring it. The leftover standing carried forward matches live leftover-join.v9 exactly, nothing is claimed closed, and required-now 28 and the DR-G21 OPEN token are correctly measured and untouched. Four imprecisions were found and are logged as observations; none falsifies a claim, misleads a recorder, or licenses any work away, so none reaches SHOULD-FIX.
